issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description indicate checkOrderReady() has a void return type (no return value expected), while the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This discrepancy can confuse students about the expected signature: they may implement a void method as described in the UML/text, while the reference uses a boolean return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to indicate checkOrderReady() returns boolean (and describe what the boolean means), or (B) change the solution implementation to declare checkOrderReady() as void (and keep any internal logic unchanged). Prefer aligning the UML/text with the intended behavior used in tests.
